summary.intent: Perform a thorough adversarial principal-engineer review of the past week's work on callisto (six open PRs plus uncommitted code), covering architecture, semantic models, performance, DX and maintainability, look for recurring issue patterns, and produce a report with remediation guidance.
summary.outcome: Delivered a prioritized report: stale version PR #248 (15 vs 32 changesets) blocked by release workflow failure fixed by #293; #290's release-source guard bypassable via workspace-inherited versions, manifest moves, and merge-only edits, and it proceeds on indeterminate observations; #291's E176 Display loses operation identity; risky Entire push_sessions config on a public repo; stale untracked selector test. Identified two recurring patterns and a recommended merge/fix order.

repo: Open PR stack: #293 (installs cargo-http-registry for release CI) fixes the failing release workflow; #290 (release-source guard) -> #291 (operation id display) -> #292 (dependency bump) are stacked; #289 duplicates #292's bump; #248 is the generated version PR.

The release workflow's test step needs cargo-http-registry via the .github/actions/install-registry-test-tools composite action; without it the release run fails in verification and the version-packages PR refresh job is skipped, leaving #248 stale while its checks stay green.

Version PR #248 (branch callisto/version-packages) was generated from 15 changesets while origin/main now has 32; merging it would ship code undescribed in the 0.12.0 changelog and trigger a later release for already-shipped changes.
Shared Git history queries use --no-merges, so changes made only in a merge resolution are invisible to the release guard; manifest renames make the move commit look like the version-setting commit.

Recurring pattern 1: treating failure as absence (ignored provider result, ignored historical parse result, unwrap_or(None) on parent-version read); code should distinguish absent / known exact / unknown.

Recurring pattern 2: using a projection of authority as authority (manifest path+version string as release source, shortened display string as operation ID, green checks on an old PR as release decision).
The history guard fetches the full manifest commit list and only then takes 100 entries, so the limit neither bounds the Git walk nor makes older version commits safe to ignore.
Entire CLI has retired Gemini support, so removal of Gemini hooks in the local settings is intentional; `$/` is valid same-repo action syntax in GitHub Actions and is not a bug.
`entire status --detailed` reports Claude Code and OpenCode hooks out of date, so adding one Claude hook did not clear the drift check.
The orin-dx/callisto GitHub repo is public, so enabling Entire push_sessions/checkpoint pushes to origin would publish prompts and redacted transcripts.

code.finding: Version lookup reads only the first canonical manifest's literal version; Cargo members using version.workspace = true yield no version commit, and manifest moves/merge-only edits evade the guard.
published_packages returns only a set, dropping provider errors and indeterminate observations, so a transient failure lets the guard proceed.

Executor's later preflight can observe the version as exact and adopt it, so the earlier source check and executor observation can disagree; the final safety decision should live at the executor boundary.
Display impl for the E176 indeterminate-observation error omits registry key, artifact slot, and platform name, so distinct uploads for the same package/version print identically.
Uncommitted change flips push_sessions from false to true and enables checkpoint pushes to a public remote.
Untracked test is on a branch older than main, expects colon selectors and bare report IDs that current main rejects or emits differently, and has six ignored discrepancy tests.

friction: GitHub API unreachable in the default sandbox, requiring retries with network access.
Heavy use of `git show` of many different commit SHAs because PR branches were stacked and moving (head OIDs had to be re-checked), making it hard to pin a stable version of the code under review.
Stale worktree branch (untracked test) predating main made it hard to treat as a current regression signal.
Entire CLI hook drift and local config changes made it unclear which local tooling changes were intentional.
open_items: Merge #293, confirm release workflow passes on main, then regenerate #248 so its decision, changelog, and consumed changesets match current main.

Rework #290's release guard around effective historical versions and an explicit source-provenance result, with tests for inherited Cargo versions, moved manifests, merge-only edits, fail-then-succeed observation, and history beyond the 100-commit limit.
Fix #291's E176 Display to include role-specific identifying fields and test two otherwise identical operations.
Restack or close duplicate dependency bumps (#289 vs #292), keeping #292 stacked only if #290 is fixed promptly.
Rebase the untracked status_version_selector_tests.rs onto current main, update its contract, and convert ignored discrepancies into active tests or tracked gaps.
Decide whether public Entire session sync is intended; otherwise revert push_sessions or use an approved private destination, and resolve Claude Code/OpenCode hook drift.
Search sibling release and history paths for the failure-as-absence pattern and measure Git call cost of the history guard on a large workspace.
